To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SME is the result of the martensite phase transformation, and the TWSME is the result of a combination of the martensitic phase transformation and the diffusion process.
the SME and TWSME in the Ti − Ni − base alloys depend on the training parameters and can be controlled by the proper selection of these parameters.
the strain−temperature training parameters (STTPs) have the strongest influence on the SME and TWSME in Ti−Ni−based alloys.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the influence of the strain − temperature training parameters (the number and the sequence of training, the temperature, the strain, the time of training, the cooling rate) on the shape memory effect and two-way shape memory effect of Ti − Ni-based alloys.
the influence of strain − temperature training parameters (STP) on shape memory effect (SM) and the two way shape memory effect (TWSME).
the effect of strain − temperature training on the shape memory properties of the alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the shape memory effect in Ti-Ni alloys can be enhanced by increasing the temperature of the training process, decreasing the strain of the training process and by decreasing the cooling rate of the training process.
the results of world studies are very different, but they are not contradictory.

the SME and the TWSME are the result of a complicated interaction of the structural and phase transformations in the alloys, which is strongly dependent on the alloy composition, the heat-treatment and the training parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no universal methods of inducing SME and TWSME in alloys of the same chemical composition.
the shape memory effect is a complex phenomenon which is not fully understood.
the shape memory effect is a phenomenon of the reversible phase transition of martensite in the austenite phase, which is accompanied by a change of shape.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two main factors that influence the shape memory effect and the two-way shape memory effect: the training procedure and the alloy composition.
the strain−temperature training procedure is the main tool for the control of the shape memory behavior in the NiTi-based shape memory alloys.

it is possible to obtain a shape memory alloy with a two-way shape memory effect by training the material at a temperature below the martensite start temperature and by applying a strain in the direction of the martensite variant that has a higher energy.
